blueprint_concepts: Position vector, distance formula, section formula
Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter) of a triangle
english: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be the points with position vectors $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}-\dfrac{2}{5}\hat{j}-\dfrac{14}{5}\hat{k}$ respectively. Then the $z$-coordinate of the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A$, $B$ तथा $C$ वे बिन्दु हैं जिनके स्थिति सदिश क्रमशः $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ तथा $\hat{i}-\dfrac{2}{5}\hat{j}-\dfrac{14}{5}\hat{k}$ हैं। तब त्रिभुज $ABC$ के लम्बकेन्द्र का $z$-निर्देशांक ______ है।
solution: $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&2\\2&1&-2\\1&-\frac25&-\frac{14}{5}\end{vmatrix}=-\dfrac{18}{5}+\dfrac{36}{5}-\dfrac{18}{5}=0$, so $O$ lies in the plane $ABC$; hence $O$ is the circumcentre
solution_full: Let $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ be the position vectors of $A$, $B$, $C$ with respect to the origin $O$.
$|\overrightarrow{a}|^2=1+4+4=9$, $|\overrightarrow{b}|^2=4+1+4=9$, $|\overrightarrow{c}|^2=1+\dfrac{4}{25}+\dfrac{196}{25}=\dfrac{225}{25}=9$. So $O$ is at distance $3$ from each vertex.
Equal distances alone do not make $O$ the circumcentre in space; $O$ must also lie in the plane of the triangle. The scalar triple product is
so $O$, $A$, $B$, $C$ are coplanar and $O$ is the circumcentre of triangle $ABC$.

On the Euler line, the centroid divides the segment from the circumcentre $O$ to the orthocentre $H$ internally in the ratio $1:2$, so $\overrightarrow{g}=\dfrac{2\cdot\overrightarrow{0}+1\cdot\overrightarrow{h}}{3}$, giving $\overrightarrow{h}=\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}+\overrightarrow{c}$.

Check: $\overrightarrow{h}-\overrightarrow{a}=3\hat{i}+\dfrac35\hat{j}-\dfrac{24}{5}\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}-\overrightarrow{c}=\hat{i}+\dfrac75\hat{j}+\dfrac45\hat{k}$; their dot product is $3+\dfrac{21}{25}-\dfrac{96}{25}=0$, so $AH\perp BC$. Similarly $(\overrightarrow{h}-\overrightarrow{b})\cdot(\overrightarrow{c}-\overrightarrow{a})=2\cdot0+\dfrac85\left(-\dfrac{12}{5}\right)+\left(-\dfrac45\right)\left(-\dfrac{24}{5}\right)=0$.
originality_note: New: a triangle in space whose vertices are equidistant from the origin and coplanar with it, so the origin is the circumcentre and the orthocentre is simply a + b + c through the Euler-line section ratio; nothing in the stem names the circumcentre (way 4, hidden configuration). Closest known: 'if the circumcentre is the origin then the orthocentre is a + b + c' as a stated result. Different because: the solver must discover that O is the circumcentre (equal lengths and a zero triple product) before using the Euler line.

concept_use.Position vector, distance formula, secti: Position vectors of the vertices, the distance formula for OA = OB = OC = 3, the centroid (a+b+c)/3 and the 1:2 section of OH by G.
concept_use.Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumce: Circumcentre (the origin), centroid and orthocentre of the triangle, linked by the Euler line H = 3G - 2O.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. The position vectors are with respect to the origin; the triangle is non-degenerate (A, B, C not collinear); the orthocentre of a triangle in space is the point of its plane where the altitudes meet, and it was checked directly. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising the origin as the circumcentre (equal distances and a zero triple product), then H = a + b + c from the Euler-line ratio.
justification: Two ideas linked: discovering the hidden circumcentre and using the Euler-line section ratio; otherwise a heavy 3D orthocentre computation. Like the 3D orthocentre work in 2026-P2-Q7 (L3).
